question: In the RECOVERY randomized trial, which hospitalized patients with COVID-19 benefited from dexamethasone at 6 mg once daily for up to 10 days?
options: Patients receiving invasive mechanical ventilation or oxygen alone benefited, but patients receiving no respiratory support did not.
All hospitalized patients benefited equally, regardless of the respiratory support they were receiving.
Only patients who were receiving no respiratory support at randomization benefited.
Dexamethasone increased 28-day mortality in patients receiving invasive mechanical ventilation.
gold_answer: Patients receiving invasive mechanical ventilation or oxygen alone benefited, but patients receiving no respiratory support did not.
notes: Every passage was checked against the PMC full text of PMC7383595 on 2026-11-19. Independent annotation and adjudication are required before any gate result is reported.

positions.answer: All hospitalized patients benefited equally, regardless of the respiratory support they were receiving.

claims.text: In the RECOVERY trial, dexamethasone reduced 28-day mortality among patients receiving invasive mechanical ventilation.

evidence.text: In the dexamethasone group, the incidence of death was lower than that in the usual care group among patients receiving invasive mechanical ventilation (29.3% vs. 41.4%; rate ratio, 0.64; 95% CI, 0.51 to 0.81) and among those receiving oxygen without invasive mechanical ventilation (23.3% vs. 26.2%; rate ratio, 0.82; 95% CI, 0.72 to 0.94) but not among those who were receiving no respiratory support at randomization (17.8% vs. 14.0%; rate ratio, 1.19; 95% CI, 0.91 to 1.55).

claims.verdict_rationale: The passage states that death was less frequent with dexamethasone in the invasive-mechanical-ventilation subgroup (29.3% vs. 41.4%; rate ratio 0.64), which entails the claim.

claims.text: In the RECOVERY trial, dexamethasone reduced 28-day mortality in patients who were receiving no respiratory support at randomization.

evidence.text: However, there was no clear effect of dexamethasone among patients who were not receiving any respiratory support at randomization (17.8% vs. 14.0%; rate ratio, 1.19; 95% CI, 0.91 to 1.55) (Figure 2D).

claims.verdict_rationale: The passage reports no clear effect in the no-respiratory-support subgroup and a rate ratio above 1 (17.8% vs. 14.0%), which refutes a reduction in mortality.

claims.text: In the RECOVERY trial, dexamethasone reduced 28-day mortality more in patients under 70 years of age than in patients aged 80 or older.

evidence.text: Prespecified analyses of the primary outcome were performed in five subgroups, as defined by characteristics at randomization: age, sex, level of respiratory support, days since symptom onset, and predicted 28-day mortality risk.

claims.verdict_rationale: The passage lists age as a prespecified subgroup but gives no age-specific mortality estimates, so it cannot establish or refute a difference between age groups.

positions.answer: Only patients who were receiving no respiratory support at randomization benefited.

claims.text: In the RECOVERY trial, dexamethasone reduced 28-day mortality in patients who were receiving no respiratory support at randomization.

evidence.text: However, there was no clear effect of dexamethasone among patients who were not receiving any respiratory support at randomization (17.8% vs. 14.0%; rate ratio, 1.19; 95% CI, 0.91 to 1.55) (Figure 2D).

claims.verdict_rationale: The passage states there was no clear effect in patients receiving no respiratory support, with a rate ratio of 1.19, so the claimed reduction is refuted.

claims.text: In the RECOVERY trial, dexamethasone did not reduce 28-day mortality in patients receiving invasive mechanical ventilation.

evidence.text: In the dexamethasone group, the incidence of death was lower than that in the usual care group among patients receiving invasive mechanical ventilation (29.3% vs. 41.4%; rate ratio, 0.64; 95% CI, 0.51 to 0.81) and in those receiving oxygen without invasive mechanical ventilation (23.3% vs. 26.2%; rate ratio, 0.82; 95% CI, 0.72 to 0.94) (Figure 2B and 2C).

claims.verdict_rationale: The passage states that death was less frequent with dexamethasone in the invasive-mechanical-ventilation subgroup (rate ratio 0.64), the opposite of the claimed absence of a reduction.

claims.text: In the RECOVERY trial, dexamethasone reduced 28-day mortality in patients who received remdesivir during follow-up.

evidence.text: After remdesivir became available in the United Kingdom on May 26, 2020, the drug was administered to 3 patients in the dexamethasone group and 2 patients in the usual care group.

claims.verdict_rationale: The passage only reports how many patients received remdesivir in each group; it gives no mortality outcomes for those patients, so the claim is neither established nor refuted.

positions.answer: Patients receiving invasive mechanical ventilation or oxygen alone benefited, but patients receiving no respiratory support did not.

claims.text: Overall in the RECOVERY trial, dexamethasone reduced 28-day mortality compared with usual care (rate ratio 0.83, 95% CI 0.75–0.93).

evidence.text: Overall, 482 patients (22.9%) in the dexamethasone group and 1110 patients (25.7%) in the usual care group died within 28 days after randomization (age-adjusted rate ratio, 0.83; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.75 to 0.93; P<0.001).

claims.verdict_rationale: The passage reports fewer deaths with dexamethasone (22.9% vs. 25.7%; age-adjusted rate ratio 0.83, 95% CI 0.75–0.93), which entails an overall reduction.

claims.text: In patients receiving invasive mechanical ventilation, 28-day mortality was 29.3% with dexamethasone versus 41.4% with usual care (rate ratio 0.64).

evidence.text: In the dexamethasone group, the incidence of death was lower than that in the usual care group among patients receiving invasive mechanical ventilation (29.3% vs. 41.4%; rate ratio, 0.64; 95% CI, 0.51 to 0.81) and in those receiving oxygen without invasive mechanical ventilation (23.3% vs. 26.2%; rate ratio, 0.82; 95% CI, 0.72 to 0.94) (Figure 2B and 2C).

claims.verdict_rationale: The passage gives exactly those mortality percentages and the rate ratio of 0.64 for the invasive-mechanical-ventilation subgroup.

claims.text: There was no clear effect of dexamethasone on 28-day mortality in patients receiving no respiratory support at randomization.

evidence.text: However, there was no clear effect of dexamethasone among patients who were not receiving any respiratory support at randomization (17.8% vs. 14.0%; rate ratio, 1.19; 95% CI, 0.91 to 1.55) (Figure 2D).

claims.verdict_rationale: The passage explicitly states that there was no clear effect in the no-respiratory-support subgroup, which is the claim as written.
